derivation.onset: Section 6.2: the earliest qualifying observation is ICE 7/10 on 2031-06-01 = Day 4 (Grade 1, no sedatives). Record Day 4 equals documented Day 4, so 7.7.
derivation.max_grade: Section 3.3 / 4.2: ICE 4/10 and awakens to voice are Grade 2. The subdural hematoma is an intracranial hemorrhage, excluded from ICANS grading (Table 6 footnote #), and headache is an excluded symptom; no edema or seizure. The highest supported grade is 2, below the record's Grade 3, so 7.3 (section 7.3, 'unsupported', A8). No documented 'not assessable' period exists, so A25 does not move it to 7.4.

ambiguity_notes: The hematoma and low platelets are not on the closed competing-cause list (A35), so the Grade 2 findings are not attributable-ambiguous under the rules. Even if a reviewer treated the hematoma as a competing cause, the unattributed highest grade would fall to Grade 1, which is still below the record's Grade 3, so both readings give 7.3 (section 7.5 same-category rule). The platelet transfusion and platelet counts are not a competing cause. The record's Grade 3 has no documented support (no seizure, no edema, ICE never 0-2).
